Web-first auto-retrying assertions, soft assertions, and polling custom conditions

BEGINNER1. Two Flavors of expect()

Playwright's expect() behaves differently depending on what you pass it:

Flavor Accepts Behavior
Web-first A Locator or Page Auto-retries on a polling interval until it passes or times out (default 5s)
Generic A plain JS value (number, string, array, object) Evaluates once, no retry — identical to Jest/Vitest 
// Web-first — retries automatically
await expect(page.getByText('Saved')).toBeVisible();

// Generic — evaluates immediately, once
expect(count).toBe(5);
expect(arr).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
⚠️ Common Pitfall: Always await web-first assertions. Without await, the check starts and the test moves on immediately — any failure is reported asynchronously (or not at all before the test ends), which is one of the most confusing bugs to diagnose in a Playwright suite.

BEGINNER2. Core Locator Assertions

await expect(locator).toBeVisible();
await expect(locator).toBeHidden();
await expect(locator).toBeEnabled();
await expect(locator).toBeDisabled();
await expect(locator).toBeChecked();
await expect(locator).toBeEditable();
await expect(locator).toBeEmpty();

Login Flow with State Assertions

test('login flow assertions', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');

  // Button disabled before input
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' })).toBeDisabled();

  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('secret');

  // Button enables after fill
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' })).toBeEnabled();
});

BEGINNER3. Text and Value Assertions

toHaveText() — full match: 
await expect(locator).toHaveText('Exact text');
await expect(locator).toHaveText(/regex/);
toContainText() — partial match: 
await expect(locator).toContainText('substring');
await expect(locator).toHaveValue('user@example.com');      // input value
await expect(locator).toHaveValues(['js', 'ts']);           // multi-select

INTERMEDIATE4. Attribute, Class, and CSS Assertions

await expect(locator).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
await expect(locator).toHaveClass('btn-primary');
await expect(locator).toHaveClass(/active/);
await expect(locator).toHaveCSS('color', 'rgb(0, 128, 0)');
await expect(locator).toHaveCount(5);
💡 Tip: toHaveClass() checks the entire class attribute string by default when passed an exact string — use a regex like /active/ to match just one class among several without listing them all.

INTERMEDIATE5. Page and Response Assertions

await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard');
await expect(page).toHaveURL(/dashboard/);
await expect(page).toHaveTitle('My App');

const response = await page.request.get('/api/health');
await expect(response).toBeOK();   // status 200-299

INTERMEDIATE6. Negation and Custom Timeouts

await expect(locator).not.toBeVisible();
await expect(locator).not.toBeChecked();

await expect(locator).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15_000 }); // override default 5s window
When to raise the timeout: a specific assertion waiting on a genuinely slow operation (a large file processing, a third-party widget loading) — not as a blanket fix for a suite that "sometimes fails." A raised timeout that papers over a real bug just makes the test slower to fail instead of fixing the flakiness.

ADVANCED7. Soft Assertions

expect.soft() records a failure without immediately stopping the test — all soft failures are collected and reported together at the end, which is invaluable when you want a complete picture of everything wrong on a page in one run instead of fixing failures one at a time.

test('profile page completeness check', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile');

  await expect.soft(page.getByTestId('avatar')).toBeVisible();
  await expect.soft(page.getByTestId('display-name')).not.toBeEmpty();
  await expect.soft(page.getByTestId('bio')).toContainText('engineer');
  await expect.soft(page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Edit profile' })).toBeVisible();

  // All four checks run regardless of earlier failures;
  // the test is marked failed at the end if any of them failed
});
⚠️ Common Pitfall: Soft assertions don't stop execution, so code that depends on a soft-failed condition (e.g. clicking an element that turned out not to be visible) can throw an unrelated hard error afterward. Use soft assertions for independent checks on the same page, not for a sequence where each step depends on the last succeeding.

ADVANCED8. expect.poll() for Custom Conditions

Web-first assertions only work on a Locator or Page. When you need to retry a custom async function — like polling a REST endpoint for a background job's status — use expect.poll().

await expect.poll(
  async () => {
    const res = await request.get('/api/job/status');
    return (await res.json()).status;
  },
  { timeout: 30_000, intervals: [2_000, 5_000, 10_000] }
).toBe('completed');

intervals lets you back off progressively — check quickly at first, then less frequently — which is friendlier to the server under test than polling at a fixed rapid rate for 30 seconds straight.

ADVANCED9. Common Pitfalls

⚠️ Pitfall 1 — Mixing up toHaveText() and toContainText(): Using toHaveText() when you meant a partial match causes assertions to fail the moment surrounding text changes even slightly (e.g. a badge count added next to a label). Use toContainText() unless you specifically need to lock down the entire string.
⚠️ Pitfall 2 — Asserting on generic values instead of the locator directly: Calling await locator.textContent() and then expect(text).toBe('Saved') loses auto-retry entirely — the text is read once, immediately, before the UI may have finished updating. Prefer await expect(locator).toHaveText('Saved') which retries the read itself.

📋 Quick Reference Summary

Concept Key Points
Web-first vs generic Locator/Page → auto-retry; plain values → one-shot, like Jest.
toHaveText vs toContainText Full match vs partial match; both accept string or RegExp.
.not Negates any assertion: expect(locator).not.toBeVisible().
Custom timeout { timeout: ms } on any web-first assertion overrides the 5s default.
expect.soft() Collects failures without stopping the test — use for independent checks.
expect.poll() Retries a custom async function when there's no locator to observe.
